# definednet_join_key (Resource)

Manages a join key: a reusable secret that enrolls any number of hosts into one network with the key's role, tags, and address prefixes. Each enrollment creates a new host named after the enrolling machine's hostname, or after the key when that is unusable; those hosts are not managed by Terraform. Use `definednet_host` instead for hosts whose identity must exist before they boot, such as lighthouses and relays.

The API key needs the `join-keys:create`, `join-keys:read`, `join-keys:update`, and `join-keys:delete` scopes, and the organization needs join keys enabled.

Only `name` and `expires_at` can change in place; any other change replaces the key, which issues a new `token` and leaves the old one unusable. Deleting a key does not remove the hosts that enrolled with it. A replacement deletes the old key before creating the new one; to rotate a key with no gap, set `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` and change `name` in the same apply, because names are unique.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One key enrolls a whole fleet; the hosts it creates are not managed by Terraform.
resource "definednet_join_key" "web" {
  name       = "web"
  network_id = definednet_network.main.id
  role_id    = definednet_role.web.id
  tags       = ["env:prod", "service:web"]

  # Give enrolled hosts an IPv4 address too; IPv6 is always assigned.
  auto_assign_cidrs = [definednet_network.main.ipv4_cidr]

  expires_at = "2027-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

# The token is a long-lived secret; hand it to your image or instance
# bootstrap the way you handle other credentials.
output "web_join_key" {
  value     = definednet_join_key.web.token
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Key name, unique within the organization: 1-54 lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen. Hosts enrolled with the key are named after it.
- `network_id` (String) Network that enrolled hosts join. Changing it replaces the key.

### Optional

- `auto_assign_cidrs` (Set of String) IPv4 prefix enrolled hosts draw addresses from: either empty or the network's own `ipv4_cidr`, which the API rejects any other prefix for. IPv6 is always assigned and is not listed here. Omit to accept the server's value, which on a dual-stack network is IPv6 only; set `[]` to assign IPv6 only explicitly. Changing it replaces the key. On a certificate version 1 network always assigns IPv4, so the API rejects `[]` there and the provider rejects it at plan time; setting `[]` needs the `networks:read` scope, because the provider reads the network to check its certificate version. When `network_id` is unknown at plan time, the check runs only during apply, after a replacement may already have deleted the old key.
- `expires_at` (String) When the key stops working, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with whole seconds, e.g. `2027-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Must be in the future when set or changed. Omit for a key that never expires.
- `role_id` (String) Role given to enrolled hosts. Changing it replaces the key.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags given to enrolled hosts, in `key:value` form. Changing them replaces the key.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Join key ID, e.g. `dnjoin-PH7SNGBJJ5MLLXOWQ7HGMRAPOQ`.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The secret hosts enroll with, `dnjoin-...`. The API returns it only when the key is created, so it is null after `terraform import`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The token is returned only on create, so it is null after import.
terraform import definednet_join_key.web dnjoin-PH7SNGBJJ5MLLXOWQ7HGMRAPOQ
```
